acts.label: Hour one
acts.story: The regional signal arrives before the damage picture, and missing towns become part of the evidence.

acts.label: The first night
acts.story: Fire, defense and liaison chains follow different signals while two collapse sites and a failed dispatch system define the night.

acts.label: Day two: the water crisis
acts.story: The aggregate picture arrives, rescue assignments move, shelters pulse and water support changes from requests to regional push.

acts.label: The turn
acts.story: Active rescues continue as the centre of gravity turns toward water and one final search meets the seventy-two-hour boundary.

milestones.headline: Outside fire units start moving before a public bulletin exists
milestones.detail: The Fire and Disaster Management Agency opened its headquarters and requested eight outside command, battalion and air resources in the earthquake minute.

milestones.headline: Five local and prefectural headquarters stand up in the earthquake minute
milestones.detail: Kumamoto and Nagasaki prefectures, Yatsushiro City, Nishiki Town and Yunomae Town recorded headquarters at 16:27.

milestones.headline: Eighteen shelter records carry the earthquake minute
milestones.detail: The archive includes thirteen Yatsushiro shelters and other community sites stamped 16:27; the matching minute is treated as a nominal response stamp, not a measured opening instant.

milestones.headline: National response offices open on a region-only intensity picture
milestones.detail: The Prime Minister's Office, National Police Agency, Cabinet Office and Digital Agency opened response bodies in the same minute.

milestones.headline: A tsunami advisory covers the Ariake and Yatsushiro seas
milestones.detail: The advisory becomes a second regional trigger while municipality-level shaking values are still unpublished.

milestones.headline: The standing instruction is damage picture, life first, timely information
milestones.detail: The Prime Minister issues the event's only numbered instruction on one region bulletin and a tsunami advisory.

milestones.headline: Hikawa opens its headquarters before a bulletin names the town
milestones.detail: Hikawa Town records its headquarters at 16:30, three minutes after the earthquake.

milestones.headline: Kumamoto is told to request support without hesitation
milestones.detail: The Ministry of Internal Affairs emails the prefecture forty-four seconds after the first municipality bulletin.

milestones.headline: Uki and Reihoku open headquarters
milestones.detail: Uki records its headquarters just over three minutes after the bulletin first names its intensity seven reading.

milestones.headline: The last municipality bulletin still has no intensity for Kashima or Kōsa
milestones.detail: Both towns remain in the bulletin's not-received category. No later municipality-level bulletin for the main shock fills the gap, so the stream preserves missing telemetry rather than inferring a shaking value.

milestones.headline: Nishihara, Hitoyoshi and Mifune open headquarters
milestones.detail: The three recorded clocks are 16:38, 16:40 and 16:55.

milestones.headline: The first national moving image reaches the crisis centre
milestones.detail: A National Police helicopter television feed from Kumamoto begins at 16:43.

milestones.headline: Defense aerial reconnaissance begins before the Governor's request
milestones.detail: The Ministry of Defense starts aerial reconnaissance forty-six minutes before the formal Ground Self-Defense Force request.

milestones.headline: Kashima's first shelter record appears while its intensity is still missing
milestones.detail: The archive stamp is not treated as a verified mayoral decision time because the feed mixes timestamp meanings.

milestones.headline: Four more headquarters stand up as shelter records spread
milestones.detail: Misato, Nagomi, Ōzu and Mashiki record headquarters; Kumamoto City, Tamana and Misato record first shelters.

milestones.headline: A second fire mobilization request follows a strong aftershock
milestones.detail: The Saga prefectural battalion is requested in the same minute as an intensity-5-lower aftershock across the southern region.

milestones.headline: The power outage reaches about 48,530 households
milestones.detail: The recorded electricity outage peak arrives forty-two minutes into the incident.

milestones.headline: Uto opens its headquarters as the first national press conference begins
milestones.detail: Uto's local response clock and the Chief Cabinet Secretary's first event briefing land in the same minute.

milestones.headline: The Governor requests Ground Self-Defense Force disaster dispatch
milestones.detail: The accepted request covers information gathering, life-saving, supply transport and living support while two town intensity values remain missing.

milestones.headline: National Route 3 closes at Hikawa for earthquake surface steps
milestones.detail: This is one of four Kumamoto closure records with a non-rounded reported minute.

milestones.headline: Kumamoto City becomes the last recorded municipal headquarters
milestones.detail: The prefecture's largest municipality records its disaster headquarters ninety-three minutes after the earthquake.

milestones.headline: The first infrastructure report sends municipal liaisons to Uki and Hikawa
milestones.detail: Five expressway routes, the Kyushu Shinkansen, seventeen conventional rail lines, airport disruption and five water-problem municipalities are recorded; the first two municipal liaison pairs follow the two intensity-seven readings.

milestones.headline: The tsunami advisory is cancelled
milestones.detail: The Ariake and Yatsushiro sea advisory ends one hour and forty-one minutes after issue.

milestones.headline: National headquarters and fire orders escalate before a casualty count exists
milestones.detail: The Prime Minister establishes the Extreme Disaster Management Headquarters and the Fire and Disaster Management Agency switches its outside-unit order from request to instruction.

milestones.headline: One town hall is unenterable and another town's network is down
milestones.detail: Misato is on emergency power with staff unable to enter; Kōsa's network is down. The other checked high-intensity municipalities report no response-work impediment.

milestones.headline: Kumamoto's disaster helicopter begins its own survey
milestones.detail: The prefectural flight starts one hour and fifty-eight minutes after the earthquake.

milestones.headline: Thirteen road closures enter the record on one rounded minute
milestones.detail: The block spans national and prefectural roads across Yatsushiro, Uki, Yamato, Mifune, Kōsa and Misato. It is labeled a batch-entry clock, not thirteen simultaneous road decisions.

milestones.headline: The Disaster Relief Act is applied to twenty-one municipalities
milestones.detail: Kumamoto Prefecture applies the act to ten cities, ten towns and one village.

milestones.headline: The first national Extreme Disaster Management Headquarters meeting begins
milestones.detail: The meeting adopts an eight-point implementation policy and records about 3,600 Self-Defense Force personnel.

milestones.headline: The prefecture splits the inbound response between Kashima and Yatsushiro
milestones.detail: An unspecified share of 149 units and 535 personnel is directed to the Kashima shopping centre; Ōita and Miyazaki battalions go to Yatsushiro; the Ground Self-Defense Force also moves toward Kashima.

milestones.headline: Yatsushiro's dispatch command system is restored
milestones.detail: The failure start and degraded procedure are not in the public record, so the replay does not invent a three-hour-thirty-three-minute outage duration.

milestones.headline: Air support and four more prefectural battalions are instructed in
milestones.detail: Miyazaki air command, Kitakyushu and Nagasaki air units are instructed at 20:15; Okayama, Hiroshima, Yamaguchi and Kagoshima battalions at 20:28.

milestones.headline: The Governor adds a Maritime Self-Defense Force request
milestones.detail: The request goes to the Sasebo District Force and is absent from the national dispatch table.

payload.recipient: Maritime Self-Defense Force Sasebo District Force

milestones.headline: JMA opens its headquarters and Saga air support is instructed
milestones.detail: JMA's headquarters begins at 21:00 and the final first-night fire air instruction goes to Saga at 21:45.

milestones.headline: Yatsushiro joins the municipal liaison list
milestones.detail: The second infrastructure report adds two officers for Yatsushiro, three hours and forty minutes after the first pair went to Uki and Hikawa.

milestones.headline: The Prime Minister and Governor share the situation
milestones.detail: They confirm close coordination between the national government and prefecture.

milestones.headline: Five hundred two shelter records carry the first day's date
milestones.detail: The archive groups 19 in the 16:00 hour, 146 in the 17:00 hour, 200 in the 18:00 hour, 96 in the 19:00 hour and 41 later. These remain record aggregates, not verified mayoral decision clocks.

milestones.headline: Four people are recovered at Kashima and ten remain unaccounted for
milestones.detail: The second prefectural meeting records rescue under way and sets a first-night instruction linking shelter or wider evacuation to delayed water supply.

milestones.headline: A Ground Self-Defense Force helicopter transfers eight civilians
milestones.detail: A UH-60 from the 8th Aviation Squadron carries the first recorded overnight patient transfer.

milestones.headline: The road snapshot is taken two hours before publication
milestones.detail: Twenty-nine observed restriction geometries are frozen; twenty-three carry a start minute and six are snapshot-only.

milestones.headline: Thirty disaster medical teams are operating in Kumamoto
milestones.detail: Eighteen teams work headquarters functions and twelve work in the field.

milestones.headline: The shelter system reaches 506 open sites and 9,186 people
milestones.detail: This is the maximum recorded shelter count; it is a prefecture aggregate and is not spatially allocated.

milestones.headline: Ground Self-Defense Force water supply begins at Yatsushiro City Hall
milestones.detail: About ten personnel with three water trailers start the first named site; seven more municipal starts follow through midday.

milestones.headline: The first national aggregate records three deaths and three active rescue incidents
milestones.detail: The report names the Yatsushiro chimney, Kashima commercial building and Hikawa houses, and carries prefecture-level evacuation-order aggregates without municipality-level clocks.

milestones.headline: The first published rescue assignments split three active incidents
milestones.detail: Yatsushiro works with Miyazaki, Kashima with Fukuoka and Hikawa with Ōita.

milestones.headline: Eight are rescued at Kashima and four of eleven at Yatsushiro
milestones.detail: The first site rescue counts enter the prefectural meeting record while work continues in Hikawa and Yatsushiro.

milestones.headline: The government survey mission reaches the Kashima damage site
milestones.detail: The mission then reaches the Kumamoto prefectural office at 13:00.

milestones.headline: Twenty-two more water trucks are arranged for regional push support
milestones.detail: Five ministry and eighteen association trucks are already committed against requests; the new pool is explicitly told not to wait for every municipality to ask.

milestones.headline: The shelter aggregate falls to 419 sites and 7,547 people
milestones.detail: The daytime point is preserved as a prefecture aggregate with no site allocation.

milestones.headline: The national posture rises to 4,600 defense, 2,000 police and 1,410 fire personnel
milestones.detail: The second national meeting also advances the ordinary local allocation tax payment.

milestones.headline: Deaths reach eight and the rescue battalion map changes
milestones.detail: Kagoshima and Okayama now work Yatsushiro; Fukuoka and Saga work Kashima. Memaru in Yamato is the one recorded isolated community.

milestones.headline: About 300 air conditioners land for shelters
milestones.detail: A C-2 brings them to Kumamoto Airport for distribution to Uki, Misato, Yatsushiro, Mifune and Uto against a 35-degree forecast.

milestones.headline: Mayors hear the first detailed two-site loss picture and an eight-municipality water allocation
milestones.detail: The meeting keeps the aggregate and site counts distinct while Ground and Maritime Self-Defense Force and Coast Guard water support spreads across eight named municipalities.

milestones.headline: Access on National Routes 3 and 57 is confirmed secured
milestones.detail: The source gives the day but no route-level reopening clock. The replay places the aggregate at the end of the day for ordering and labels that placement; it does not invent a reopening time.

milestones.headline: The defense posture reaches about 4,600 people and 29 aircraft
milestones.detail: Four of five Maritime Self-Defense Force vessels reach Yatsushiro Port; about 170 people work Kashima and 30 to 40 work the Yatsushiro mill.

milestones.headline: Shelter occupancy reaches its recorded peak of 9,931
milestones.detail: The peak occupant count occurs across 419 shelters, fewer than at the 506-shelter maximum; the two peaks are not conflated.

milestones.headline: The Ground Self-Defense Force states the rescue-to-water condition
milestones.detail: Twenty-two Emergency Fire Response Team rescues are recorded with three operations still running; after life-saving ends, the centre of gravity will move to water supply.

milestones.headline: The rescue tally reaches 98 rescued and 620 transported
milestones.detail: Local fire headquarters and Emergency Fire Response Teams strike the aggregate since the earthquake.

milestones.headline: Heat-stroke prevention becomes an explicit response task
milestones.detail: The Fire and Disaster Management Agency begins messaging through social media and leaflets.

milestones.headline: The national headquarters decides to create an on-site command
milestones.detail: The on-site Extreme Disaster Management Headquarters is established at the Kumamoto prefectural office thirty minutes later.

milestones.headline: Ten of eleven are out at Yatsushiro and twelve at Kashima
milestones.detail: The last Yatsushiro rescue requires heavy machinery that cannot reach the site while the new national on-site headquarters occupies the same disaster prevention centre.

milestones.headline: Water supply reaches 24 sites with 32 vehicles
milestones.detail: The defense posture is about 5,100 people while search teams remain at Kashima, Yatsushiro and Hikawa.

milestones.headline: Three hundred ninety-nine shelters hold 9,637 people
milestones.detail: Evacuation instructions widen again and fifty-six disaster medical teams operate; all values remain report aggregates.

milestones.headline: The prefecture holds its seventh headquarters meeting
milestones.detail: This is the last prefectural-only morning meeting before the national and prefectural bodies meet jointly.

milestones.headline: A renewed joint search runs at Kashima against the seventy-two-hour mark
milestones.detail: The Self-Defense Forces, police and fire service run the search during the day. The source gives no clock, so noon is only a labeled display placement.

milestones.headline: Water support reaches 41 sites with 49 vehicles
milestones.detail: The same day pairs the expanded water network with the final Kashima search; the public record does not publish a complete personnel split.

milestones.headline: National on-site and prefectural headquarters meet together
milestones.detail: The on-site body's first meeting is the prefecture's eighth; from here the two bodies meet jointly.

milestones.headline: The first seventy-two hours close with rescue and water both still active
milestones.detail: The replay stops at the exact incident-plus-seventy-two-hours boundary. Later returns, designations and long recovery remain outside this stream.
